items.article_context_en: Real-world assets already back the largest stablecoins, yet borrowing against them onchain still runs through variable-rate pools. Peter Gaffney of O2O Capital Partners explains why fixed-rate, fixed-term lending is the missing piece, and how a 5% shift in Sky and Ethena reserves could create $1.8 billion of demand for real-world assets. …and if you’re looking for more institutional insights: ETF Central’s Trackinsight Global ETF Survey 2026, produced with Calamos Investments and S&P Dow Jones Indices, finds nearly 7 in 10 professional investors are reassessing their ETF holdings. Plus, CoinDesk’s latest Digital Assets Quarterly Report is out now. Fixed-rate lending is the clearest growth lever for real-world assets (RWAs) in decentralized finance (DeFi). It unlocks a strategy that credit desks have run for decades but DeFi has never meaningfully implemented: buy a quality income asset, borrow against it at a locked rate below the asset’s yield and buy more of the asset. Stablecoins are steadily sitting around $300 billion in supply and aggregate vault assets are nearing the $20 billion milestone. Morpho alone carries more than $16 billion in deposits, most of it in variable-rate markets priced on pool utilization, which serve crypto-native traders who manage liquid positions in real time but leave longer-dated borrowers with uncertainty. Fixed-rate, fixed-term lending closes that gap by matching the term of the loan to the duration of the collateral, especially for RWAs whose redemptions can settle anywhere from T+7 to T+90. With the borrow cost and maturity known at entry, institutional counterparties can underwrite an RWA looping vault the same way they approve conventional term financing. This is the same bedrock foundation that formed and grew traditional credit markets to $51 trillion in US fixed income versus $1.6 trillion in floating-rate leveraged loans. The move to fixed rates is already underway: Morpho recently opened fixed-rate, fixed-term markets through Morpho Midnight, which Coinbase used to launch fixed-rate crypto-backed loans to its customers in September 2026. DeFi is a battle-tested real-time execution engine with a narrow collateral base of volatile crypto assets that move by magnitudes in stress. This is what turned the October 10, 2025 liquidation cascade into a $19 billion event, marking the start of a nearly 60% reduction in DeFi total value locked for the eight months to follow.

items.article_context_en: Vault12 raised $17.45 million selling VGT in 2018 and says it met or dropped every promise, yet the token has never traded on a centralized exchange. The issuer of a cryptocurrency token that has never traded on a major exchange has presented an early test of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) proposed safe harbor framework. Crypto wallet backup firm Vault12, backed by Winklevoss Capital and Naval Ravikant, warned that the SEC’s proposed token safe harbor could leave exchanges unwilling to list tokens because of the risk of a later regulatory challenge. The safe harbor is part of the SEC’s Regulation Crypto Assets proposal, issued in August to establish conditions under which a token would no longer be subject to its original investment contract. Vault 12 raised $17.45 million from 38 investors through agreements for future tokens in 2018 and detailed how Vault Guardian Token (VGT) has never traded on a centralized exchange, it said in in a comment letter on Tuesday. The letter presents questions about the SEC’s proposed path for older crypto projects to move their tokens out of securities treatment. Vault12 says its 2018 token sale fits that path almost exactly: it has fulfilled or formally abandoned every commitment in its white paper, yet its token has never been listed. Its concerns echo a comment letter from industry group The Digital Chamber, which Vault12 says it supports. Exchanges Vault12 approached about listing VGT wanted assurance that the SEC would not later challenge the token’s status, according to the letter. The company argued that the proposed safe harbor does not provide enough certainty for them to proceed. The SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets would create exemptions for token fundraising and a conditional safe harbor for ending an investment contract associated with a token. To use the safe harbor, issuers would have to complete or permanently stop promised essential managerial efforts, make no new such commitments and have no intention of doing so. They would also file a transition report, known as Form TR, explaining their conclusion, according to the SEC’s proposal.

items.article_context_en: 21, 2026 Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 options are taking a bigger share of the largest cryptocurrency’s derivatives market in a sign that trading is becoming more sophisticated. According to Volmex, the issuer of the bitcoin volatility index BVIV, options accounted for just under 60% of open interest among all bitcoin derivatives last week. That’s up from around 50% at the start of the year. Open interest is the total value of contracts that traders have opened and not yet closed. The market encompasses bitcoin futures, perpetual futures and both bitcoin-native and ETF-based options. Volmex called the growth a structural shift in bitcoin markets, a sign that trading bitcoin is now about managing risk, not just betting on direction. Options allow investors to hedge their holdings, earn additional income or bet on a big move without borrowing, so positions can last longer than a leveraged perpetual bet. They are also priced on expected volatility, which is what gauges like Vomex’s BVIV track. Options are derivative contracts with a fixed expiry date that let traders bet on three things at once. They can bet on the direction of the price, on how big the swings will be and on timing, meaning by when a move will or won't happen. As of Friday, the bitcoin derivatives market looked like this: Options tied to U.S. bitcoin exchange-traded funds had about $36 billion in open interest, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for nearly $35 billion of the total. Add in options on crypto-native platforms, and the figure rises to roughly $76 billion. When bitcoin futures, including perpetual futures and dated contracts, are taken into account, the overall market reaches about $129 billion.

items.article_context_en: Independent committees are assessing a potential tie-up, while strong SpaceX earnings lift shares ahead of Tesla’s results. SpaceX SPCX$159.39·Market Closed and Tesla TSLA$386.48·Market Closed are exploring a potential merger, Elon Musk, the CEO and a shareholder of both companies, said on Tuesday, raising the prospect of combining two of his biggest companies and more than 30,000 bitcoin BTC$84,459.46. Musk owns about 36% of space and AI-focused SpaceX outright, rising to 48.4% including restricted shares and unexercised options, according to a June filing. His reported beneficial ownership of electric-car maker Tesla is 19.8%, including restricted compensation shares. Speaking during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call, Musk said both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to assess a tie-up. A combination would unite SpaceX’s reported 18,712 BTC and Tesla’s 11,509 BTC, for a total of 30,221 BTC. “Do I think it would be a good idea, yes. But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he said. His interests in both companies prevent him from participating in committee discussions. “It's an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can't be in the conversation,” Musk said. “The special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction.” SpaceX shares jumped abpit 9% to $161 in Wednesday’s premarket trading. Revenue of $14.58 billion exceeded the $12.7 billion consensus, while earnings per share of 35 cents beat the 15-cent forecast. Capital expenditure reached $19.59 billion, including $16.44 billion for AI. The results helped revive battered AI stocks.

items.article_context_en: The Series A round, which included participation from North Island Ventures and existing investors, brings New York-based Mural's total funding to $28 million. Tether led a $15 million funding round in Mural, expanding the stablecoin issuer’s investments in technology that enables AI agents to handle payments. The Series A round, which included participation from North Island Ventures and existing investors, brings New York-based Mural's total funding to $28 million, according to an emailed announcement on Tuesday. Mural, founded by former Palantir (PLTR) engineers, provides fintechs and other platforms with infrastructure for managing accounts, payments, identity verification and regulatory compliance across traditional banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include payroll platform Deel and browser developer Opera. The funding comes as financial technology companies explore “agentic finance,” in which AI systems can initiate and execute transactions on behalf of individuals or businesses. Mural's infrastructure allows companies to set transaction limits, restrict counterparties and require additional approvals for larger payments, addressing questions around authorization and accountability when autonomous software moves money. “As agents start moving money, that connection to the banks, payment networks and compliance systems the world still runs on becomes essential,” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in the statement. The investment reflects Tether's growing interest in infrastructure beyond stablecoin issuance, particularly as programmable payments emerge as a potential use case for AI-powered financial services. items.article_context_en: Eight secret keys at eMudhra, an Indian firm that vouches for websites, were compromised. Browsers and software makers are rushing out fixes. The internet has been scrambling to patch a hole in the system that tells your browser which websites are real. The risk is general and falls mostly on people running outdated softwares, crypto users included. 17, when a researcher told browser makers that eight secret keys at eMudhra, an Indian company that vouches for websites, have been compromised. A researcher named Wayne reported the security flaw and to prove the vulnerability, he used all eight compromised keys to digitally sign his warning message: "We have a problem here – Wayne." When a user visits a website, their browser checks a digital certificate to confirm the site is real. Companies called certificate authorities issue those certificates, and eMudhra is one of them. It has issued more than 60 million certificates, according to The Register. Each certificate authority signs its certificates with a private key. If someone steals or cracks that stamp, they can forge authentic-looking certificates for any website. Crypto users could also be affected, though mainly outside the browser. Exchange bots, trading scripts and wallet backends often run on Python, Node or Go, and a forged certificate for an exchange’s API could in theory let an attacker on the same network read or alter a bot’s traffic. No crypto attacks have been reported so far. But according to Mudit Gupta, chief technology officer at Polygon Labs, the bigger concern is not crypto itself, it is outdated software.

items.article_context_en: Strong results from SpaceX and Super Micro sent Asian chip stocks surging, and ZEC led crypto higher after developers set a date for its next network upgrade. Bitcoin rose 1.3% to just above $82,700 as of Wednesday Asian morning hours, hovering around the $83,000 mark after strong earnings from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer revived the AI trade and sent tech stocks across Asia higher. ZEC led the majors, jumping 11% to about $1,260, after Zcash developers set the mainnet activation height for NU7, the network’s next upgrade. The activation height is the block number at which every node switches to the new rules. NU7 cuts the time between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, so payments confirm three times faster, and sends 60% of transaction fees into a reserve that’s paid out over time. It’s been running on Zcash’s test network since early October. HYPE and DOGE each gained more than 3%, XRP added nearly 3% to $1.33, and ether rose 2% to about $2,450. BNB and SOL gained between 1% and 2%, while TRX was flat, according to CoinDesk data. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 3.7% and Taiwan’s Taiex gained 1.4%. SpaceX rose 8% in extended trading and Super Micro jumped 16%, and Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1%. It wasn’t all good news for the AI buildout, however, as Australian data-center developer Nextdc crashed 40% after it cut its outlook. Brent rose above $110 a barrel as attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz threatened shipments and U.S. industry data pointed to another drop in stockpiles. The dollar firmed a touch, and Treasuries gave back some of Tuesday’s gains.
